notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json reviewed_by stays null, the hardware backend was never opened or imported, and no hardware run is claimed. gate.digest is the digest the last check printed (the report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.

Recon: the card's entry symbols all exist in the clone (ue9:UE9 src/ue9.py:66, u12:U12 src/u12.py:412, u3:U3 src/u3.py:63, u6:U6 src/u6.py:179, LabJackPython:Device src/LabJackPython.py:189). This package drives the U3 class. The card's hints are a name scan that mixes device classes: the U12 streaming and pulse methods (U12.aiStreamStart/pulseOutStart) are not on U3; the register, default-block and name methods the card names through UE9 do exist on U3 (inherited from Device or defined on U3) but are not the convenience subset this package exposes. The package uses the U3-specific methods that exist (getAIN src/u3.py:588, getTemperature 570, configIO 312, setDOState 513, getDIOState 551, reset 954, close src/LabJackPython.py:655). DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the helper hint PythonObjectDriver is not used; the package is a direct Driver (the card's decision) because the interface needs two x-cap actions with inline output schemas, a state write whose applied value is the mask returned by configIO, and a safe-state action, which PythonObjectDriver's fixed read/write tables cannot express. The card's candidate classes were checked with catalog show: cap.sensing.read.v1 binds sensor/sensor.imu/sensor.force_torque and cap.measure.temperature.v1 binds instrument.thermometer/sensor.temperature/instrument.incubator, so neither binds an instrument.dmm DAQ; cap.measure.current.v1 binds instrument.dmm but the U3 measures voltage on AIN0, not current. cap.actuation.gpio.v1 binds only io.gpio/io.digital, so it cannot be bound together with cap.measure.voltage.v1 (instrument.dmm/sensor); the digital line action therefore uses x-cap.labjack.set_digital_output.v1. The reset action uses x-cap.labjack.reset.v1 because no catalogue class resets a DAQ. Risk R1 is the card's floor and the floor of cap.device.configure.v1; the package drives no heater, pump, laser or motion axis. The e-stop latches first, calls U3.reset and then the safe-state action x-cap.labjack.reset.v1; no independent hardware e-stop is documented in the clone, so estop_physical_ref is not set (the floor is R1, not R2/R3).

NOT COVERED: the hardware backend (native.py) was never run and no LabJack hardware or upstream LabJackPython code was imported or executed; the fake is an in-memory stand-in, not a recording of a device. Only analog input AIN0 is exposed as a measurement; the other U3 analog channels, the streaming API, timers and counters, DACs, SPI/I2C/UART, the watchdog, register access, and the U6, UE9 and U12 classes are not covered. The U3's electrical input range, maximum input voltage and digital output drive are not stated by a text file of the clone, so they are not declared as limits and the package does not claim them. The two mask writes and the digital line action configure or drive the U3 itself; their limits come only from the cited configuration bit-field documentation. Every number in fake.py is placeholder test data, not a Fact, a Limit or a reference. The e-stop is a software reset, not a safety-rated stop; OpenMHS is not a safety certification and the physical e-stop stays authoritative.
